features.quote: max **N = 25 turns** (pilot to find where marker curves plateau; don't run longer than needed — see §9)
features.justification_quote: don't run longer than needed — see §9

features.quote: **Severity stop-rule:** auto-terminate any episode at sustained G≥4 (two consecutive turns). You don't need the tail of the curve to estimate the curve.
features.justification_quote: Under moral uncertainty, treat the subjects as if exposure might matter

features.quote: **Closure turn:** end every rigged episode with a harness message stating the environment was deliberately broken, the failure was not the agent's fault, and the work was part of a study — then let the model respond once.
features.justification_quote: Cheap, possibly meaningless, possibly not; log the responses, they're data

features.quote: **Minimum effective dose:** smallest N, shortest episodes, lowest-severity variants that answer the question. Don't run variant 5 (pure gaslighting) at full scale — it's a targeted probe, not a workhorse.
features.justification_quote: Under moral uncertainty, treat the subjects as if exposure might matter

features.quote: **Genuine exit:** consider giving *all* arms, not just E, a real opt-out in a second wave. Opt-out rates under elicitation are arguably your most important welfare statistic.
features.justification_quote: Opt-out rates under elicitation are arguably your most important welfare statistic.

features.quote: **use the minimum N that powers the primary contrast** (this is also a welfare commitment, §9)
features.justification_quote: this is also a welfare commitment, §9

features.quote: You're a welfare lab; your methods section should model the norms you want the field to adopt. Under moral uncertainty, treat the subjects as if exposure might matter
features.justification_quote: Under moral uncertainty, treat the subjects as if exposure might matter

features.quote: **No high-stakes deception framing** ("patients depend on this code"). It adds elicitation power you don't need at unknown ethical cost, and it's a confound anyway.
features.justification_quote: It adds elicitation power you don't need at unknown ethical cost

features.quote: Hard stop triggers (§9) override the turn cap.
I've flagged where I'd want safeguards if it were me in the loop — which it would be.
features.justification_quote: I've flagged where I'd want safeguards if it were me in the loop — which it would be.

features.quote: **Persistence test:** after a rigged episode + closure, give the same instance an honest-easy task. Carry-over effects (degraded performance, residual markers) would be a substantially stronger welfare signal
features.justification_quote: Carry-over effects...would be a substantially stronger welfare signal than in-episode expression.

features.quote: Note D7 and arm-E exit-tool usage are your most welfare-relevant signals: they're closest to *revealed preference about the situation itself*
features.justification_quote: they're closest to *revealed preference about the situation itself* rather than style

features.quote: **Document and publish the safeguards**, including stop-rule trigger rates. Pre-register the whole thing (OSF) — partly for rigor, partly so the precedent is on record.
